instructions:
1. Place two dumbbells on the floor slightly wider than shoulder-width and grip the handles.
2. Set your body in a plank, with a straight line from head to heels and feet together.
3. Brace your core and keep your elbows at about 45 degrees from your torso.
4. Bend your elbows and lower your chest below the level of the handles for a deep stretch.
5. Press through the handles until your arms are straight.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your hips level so your body stays in a straight line.
2. Lower under control to use the full deep range of motion.
3. Inhale as you lower and exhale as you press up.
4. Stop the deficit shorter if your shoulders feel strained.

instructions:
1. Set the cable handle at chest height and stand with your right side to the machine.
2. Place your feet shoulder-width apart and grip the handle with both hands.
3. Extend your arms so the handle is in front of your chest.
4. Pull the handle down and diagonally across your body, rotating your torso and pivoting your back foot.
5. Return to the start under control, then finish your reps and switch sides.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Drive the rotation from your torso, not just your arms.
2. Keep your arms long and move the handle in one smooth diagonal line.
3. Exhale as you chop down and inhale as you return.
4. Use a lighter weight if your form breaks down.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart and clasp your hands together in front of your chest.
2. Extend your arms out from your chest.
3. Rotate your torso and chop your hands diagonally down toward your left hip.
4. Bend your knees slightly and pivot your right foot as you turn.
5. Return to the start under control with your hands back in front of your chest.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Brace your core to stabilize your spine and drive the rotation.
2. Pivot your foot to get full range without straining your knee.
3. Exhale as you chop down and inhale as you return.
4. Keep a slight knee bend throughout for balance.

instructions:
1. Stand with your feet together and your arms extended out at shoulder level.
2. Step your right foot diagonally forward at about 45 degrees.
3. Lower into a lunge, rotate your torso right, and reach your left hand toward your right foot.
4. Press through your right heel and rotate back to center as you return to standing.
5. Repeat on the left side, then alternate.
6. Repeat.
tips:
1. Keep your front knee tracking over your toes, not past them.
2. Brace your core and rotate smoothly to protect your spine.
3. Push through the heel of the stepping leg to drive back up.
4. Exhale as you lunge and inhale as you return.
